title: observability: token-level KV metrics, cost/latency dashboards, and alert tuning
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: production incidents in Jan-Feb showed regressions in token-level unit economics when KV cache hit-rate dropped. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, per-token cost and latency breakdowns, Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerts to detect regressions early.

Summary of changes: added instrumentation for KV cache hit/miss with aggregation by model, route, and region; emit token-level latency (encode, kv_lookup, decode) and per-token cost estimate (based on current pricing model) to the metrics pipeline; new Grafana dashboards that show cost/latency composition and rollout-aware panels; OpenTelemetry tracing hooks for per-token spans to correlate cache misses with tail latency; alert tuning for cache-hit-rate, token-cost-per-minute, and tail-p95 token latency.

Implementation notes: all instrumentation is behind a feature flag (observability.token_metrics_v2) to allow staged rollout. Metrics emitted via our existing metrics library as prometheus-compatible counters/gauges/histograms: redwood_kv_cache_hit_total, redwood_kv_cache_miss_total, redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood_token_cost_cents_total (estimate). Traces use existing OTEL collector; added token-span attributes: token_index, kv_hit, model, route. Grafana dashboards are stored in observability/dashboards/token_metrics_v2.json and use templating for model/route/region. Alert rules added to prometheus/rules/token_observability.rules.yml.

Backwards compatibility: no change to public APIs; metrics are additive. Existing dashboards continue to work. Feature flag default is off for all tenants; rollout planned to internal + canary + gradual prod.

Testing: unit tests for metrics hooks and cost computation; integration tests in perf-canary to validate metrics throughput and low overhead; end-to-end smoke on staging with synthetic traffic for model/generation patterns. Load impact: measured ~2% CPU and ~1.5% memory increase at 90th percentile in perf-canary for token_metrics_v2 on a medium workload.

Migration and rollout plan: enable for internal and SRE-owned Dedicated clusters for 48h, validate dashboard signals and alert noise, then enable on 10% of prod requests for two days, followed by full rollout if no regressions. All changes reversible by disabling the feature flag.

Checklist:
- [x] Add metrics and tracing instrumentation behind feature flag
- [x] Implement token cost estimator and expose as metric
- [x] Create Grafana dashboards and templated panels
- [x] Add Prometheus alert rules with tuned thresholds and silences
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Perf-canary run and load verification

Related: ENG-3421 (token economics alerting), ENG-3509 (kv-cache observability improvements).

review_comments: Jordan Reyes: Please confirm cardinality controls on token tags (model/route) to avoid high metric cardinality.
Priya Nair (author): We cap route/model label combinations and sample token-level traces to 1% by default; documented limits in docs/observability/token-level-metrics.md.
Luis Martinez: Can we make alert thresholds configurable per-customer? Some dedicated customers have low cache hit-rate baselines.
Priya Nair (author): Alerts are templated and support per-tenant overrides via prometheus relabel configs; noted in alert rules comments.
Asha Kapoor: The dashboard panels look good — please add a panel that attributes cost to model version for quick rollback decisions.
Priya Nair (author): Added a model_version breakdown panel and unit tests that validate its query returns expected series in staging.
release_notes: Adds token-level KV cache metrics, token latency buckets, and a token-cost estimator. New Grafana dashboards and tuned Prometheus alerts for cache-hit-rate and token-level latency/cost. Feature-flagged rollout. No breaking changes.
